verdict.rationale: Jitsu's core design streams event data into warehouses and storage you own (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS), keeps profiles there, and is 100% open-source and self-hostable. That makes leaving plausible without data being trapped in Jitsu. However, there is no documented explicit 'export all my data' feature or stated open file format, and nothing on exporting data from the Jitsu Cloud-provisioned ClickHouse. The Management API and CLI manage configuration, but no config export or backup is documented. Missing for 10: a documented full-export or offboarding path (including Cloud-provisioned ClickHouse data and workspace configuration), named open export formats, and independent corroboration of migrating off Jitsu.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Make your data warehouse the single source of truth for your data.
Delivery to destinations — ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS, and dozens of SaaS tools
in ClickHouse, which Jitsu Cloud provisions for you, or in your own BigQuery, Snowflake or Redshift.
Profiles are customer records stored in your warehouse, based on the events data you send to Jitsu.
Jitsu is 100% open-source and can be deployed to any on-premise infrastructure.
Jitsu exposes an HTTP API for managing workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions.
